summary: pricing-engine quote latency (p99 60ms -> >2s, deadline-exceeded) is a downstream symptom. At ~13:22 the redis-cache primary node (redis-cache-2) failed health checks and failover promoted redis-cache-3, which was mid-resync with an EMPTY dataset. redis-cache memory fell 70%->8% and hit ratio 96%->14%. The cold cache triggered market-data-service 'cache miss storm' events, rebuilding each quote from the exchange feed snapshot in 1-8s, raising market-data-service p99 from ~40ms to ~1980ms and cascading into pricing-engine's quote computation. No trading-service deploys or config changes occurred; request rate was flat and exchange-gateway was healthy, ruling out capacity saturation, bad deployment and external-provider failure. Root cause category: infrastructure_failure at redis-cache. Matches historical incident HIST-107 (empty-replica-promotion cold cache storm).

ranked_hypotheses.title: redis-cache primary failure promoted an empty (resyncing) replica, cold-cache storm on market-data-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 13:22 the redis-cache primary node redis-cache-2 failed health checks; automatic failover promoted replica redis-cache-3, which was mid-resync and had an empty dataset. The resulting cold cache caused market-data-service cache-miss storms (rebuilding quotes from the exchange feed, taking seconds), slowing market-data-service and cascading through pricing-engine quote computation to produce 2-3s quote latency.

causal_chain.claim: redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 failed health checks (3 PING timeouts)
failover promoted an empty resyncing replica -> cache dataset lost (memory 70%->8%, hit ratio 96%->14%)
market-data-service cache-miss storm: rebuild quotes from exchange feed, 1-8s each
pricing-engine quote computation deadline exceeded calling market-data-service; p99 ~60ms->2227ms

assumptions: The empty dataset was the cause of the miss storm, not a coincidental eviction (evictions/CPU flat support this).
No other dependency of market-data-service degraded simultaneously (exchange-gateway healthy).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation of market-data-service / redis under load
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Quote load outgrew provisioned cache/processing capacity, exhausting resources and causing slow quote rebuilds.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service request_rate flat at ~950 req/s (F7); redis evictions and CPU flat (F10); redis memory and hit ratio fell rather than saturated (F3).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Faulty code/config release or external provider failure
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A deployment or config change to a trading service, or exchange-gateway degradation, introduced the latency.

causal_chain.claim: faulty change deployed to a trading service

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: No deployments/config changes to any trading service (only unrelated auth-service v7.2.0); exchange-gateway p99 flat ~130ms with zero errors.

facts.statement: pricing-engine p99 rose from ~60ms to a 2227.82ms max in the 13:12 bucket and stayed elevated through 14:48.
redis-cache primary redis-cache-2 failed its health check and failover promoted an empty, resyncing replica redis-cache-3.
redis-cache memory_pct fell to ~8% and hit_ratio_pct to ~14% in the 13:24 bucket.
market-data-service emitted 204 'cache miss storm' warnings rebuilding quotes from the exchange feed snapshot in 1-8s.
pricing-engine's dominant error was 'quote computation deadline exceeded: market-data-service took <n>ms' (72 occurrences, up to 8456ms).
market-data-service p99 rose in lockstep to 1979.98ms max in the 13:12 bucket.
market-data-service request_rate stayed flat (~950 req/s), and redis-cache evictions (~3/min) and cpu (~22%) stayed flat.
exchange-gateway had no errors and flat p99 (~130ms).
No deployments or config changes affected any trading service; only auth-service v7.2.0 was deployed at 11:30.
A prior incident (HIST-107) was an empty-replica-promotion cold cache storm affecting the same services.

timeline.event: Unrelated auth-service v7.2.0 deploy (session cookie hardening).
pricing-engine and market-data-service p99 begin climbing (60ms->421ms / 40ms->353ms).
redis-cache-2 fails health check (3 PING timeouts), marked primary down.
Failover promotes empty resyncing replica redis-cache-3 to primary.
First pricing-engine 'quote computation deadline exceeded' error.
redis-cache client reconnect storm begins (15048 new connections/10s).
Latency still recovering (pricing-engine p99 avg 1170ms; redis hit ratio 45.78%).

recommended_actions.action: Warm/repopulate redis-cache immediately (preload hot quote keys from market-data-service) to cut the ongoing miss storm and restore hit ratio.
recommended_actions.rationale: Hit ratio is still only ~46% at 14:48 and latency remains elevated; warming the cache is the direct mitigation.

recommended_actions.action: Investigate why redis-cache-2 failed health checks (PING timeouts) and why redis-cache-3 was mid-resync at failover time.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failover promoted a replica with an empty dataset; root fix is ensuring replicas are fully synced/healthy before promotion.

recommended_actions.action: Add replica-sync verification/guard to the failover procedure so promotion is refused or delayed when the target replica's dataset is empty or resyncing.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents repeating the empty-replica promotion that caused this incident (same pattern as HIST-107).

recommended_actions.action: Add cache-miss-storm alerting on redis-cache hit_ratio and on market-data-service miss-storm log rate to catch cold-cache onset before it cascades.
recommended_actions.rationale: Detection lagged: miss storm began 13:22 but p99 alarm/report came later; early detection shortens impact.

data_gaps: redis-cache has no 'restarts' metric (tc-019 not_found), so process restart count for the failed primary could not be confirmed directly.
No infra/host telemetry for the redis-cache nodes (only cache-level metrics); the root cause of the primary's PING timeouts (host failure, network partition, OOM-kill) is not observable here.
market-data-service log query returned truncated=true and archives rows only from 09:00 onward; message-level coverage is incomplete though the top-pattern count (204) is consistent.
Deployment listing returned only one entry and initially partial (shard timeout); cannot fully exclude an undocumented deploy, though config-change list was complete and empty.
